A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison; image-based figure content was inspected visually.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-description benchmarks, randomization checks, percentile analyses, and a human annotation pilot involving six features.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds cluster-count and language-model ablations, activation analyses, and a seven-participant human study.

M1.justification: The percentile-sampling, embedding and k-means clustering, and LLM-labeling pipeline remains unchanged, as do its core scoring procedures. Alternative cluster counts and language models are tested as ablations rather than introduced as a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Human evaluation shifts from an author-only pilot to independent PhD and working-student participants from two institutions, broadening the evaluated population. The English C4, Cosmopedia, and concept-specific text coverage and feature-description tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmarks retain GPT-Explain and Output-Centric with the same model-specific participation. The new evaluation-generator ablation reuses GPT-Explain; Qwen3, Phi-4, and DeepSeek R1 serve as pipeline components rather than new competing feature-description methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols varying k across 1, 3, 5, and 10 and changing the LLM used separately for description generation and evaluation. Human evaluation expands from one annotator and six features to seven annotators and eight features, and adds embedding-based comparison of human descriptions. The original benchmark settings remain documented as before.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.5 add cluster-count sensitivity and separate generator/evaluator ablations. Appendix A.6 adds relative-activation distributions and cluster-level examples testing whether percentile sampling captures meaningful patterns. The earlier randomization and quartile analyses are retained and consolidated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 6 newly reports between-participant variability through boxplots of human ratings and human-description cosine similarities, replacing the pilot's individual-rating presentation. The existing 95% AUC confidence intervals and MAD standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no new repeated-run or significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: The main benchmark values are unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 1, but substantial ablation, activation-analysis, and human-study results are added. For example, v3 Table 3 reports maximum/mean AUC of 0.75/0.75 at k=1 and 0.88/0.61 at k=10, versus 0.85/0.65 at k=5. Polysemanticity results also change: Figure 5 revises GPT-2 XL feature 6067's PRISM score from 0.41 to 0.38.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the formal relative-activation ratio r_j = |a_99/a_max| in Equation 9. The earlier extraction and scoring mathematics is substantively retained, with indexing, embedding notation, and control/concept labeling clarified rather than new theoretical results or proofs added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the critique of existing feature-description methods to automated neuron-level methods for LLMs/NLP and qualifies the single-description comparison. The three central contributions—multi-concept descriptions, quantitative evaluation, and feature analysis—and the main accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 replaces v1's proprietary-model necessity argument with open-model applicability, interprets the new ablations as robustness evidence, and develops a precision-versus-fragmentation explanation for increasing k. It adds fixed-cluster incompleteness and MAD's outlier sensitivity as limitations, and uses relative-activation diagnostics to support percentile sampling.

D1.justification: Appendix A.8 and Figure 16 add participant recruitment, compensation, completion-time information, and full study instructions. Appendix A.5 supplies identifiers and access links for the alternative generators. Existing generation prompts, benchmark implementation details, GPU and timing disclosures, and PRISM code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Neo et al.'s attention–MLP interaction work and the Qwen3, Phi-4, and DeepSeek R1 reports. It also qualifies its positioning toward automated neuron-level NLP interpretation. The related-work discussion and representative-method overview are otherwise substantially retained.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the abstract, scoring explanation, human-study summary, and limitations. It condenses the main-text sanity checks into a summary, consolidates their details in Appendix A.6, and moves some concept-space discussion to Appendix A.7. The overall section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reformats the document's typography, title treatment, running headers, and figure sizing. It adds four tables and three figures, revises the human-comparison display, changes plot axes and legends, reorders benchmark rows, and relocates the sanity-check table to the appendix. Existing metalabel displays are retained with revised layout.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves cluster-count sensitivity as future work, asserts model requirements without quantitative ablations, and bases human validation on one co-author. v3 addresses these important validation gaps through targeted ablations and a documented study with seven independent participants. These substantially strengthen the evidence, although robustness wording remains overstated: Table 5 shows maximum AUC changing from 0.85 with Gemini evaluation to 0.58 with Qwen3 evaluation.
